Finnish

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Proto-Finnic *vanha (compare Estonian vana), from Proto-Uralic *wanša (compare Komi-Zyrian важ (važ), Udmurt вуж (vuž)).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈʋɑnhɑ/, [ˈʋɑ̝nhɑ̝]
  • Rhymes: -ɑnhɑ
  • Syllabification(key): van‧ha
  • Hyphenation(key): van‧ha

Adjective

[edit]

vanha (comparative vanhempi, superlative vanhin)

  1. old (of age)
    Synonym: iäkäs
    Antonyms: nuori (“young”) (of people, animals, etc. and occasionally also of things), uusi (“new”) (of things)
    Isäni on jo hyvin vanha, äitiä paljon vanhempi, melkein jo vanhus.
    My father is already quite old, much older than my mother, almost an old man.
    Pekka ajaa vanhalla autonromulla.
    Pekka drives an old beater.
  2. old, former
    Synonym: entinen
    Vanha asunto meni vaihdossa.
    I traded out my old apartment.
  3. expired
    Synonyms: vanhentunut, (of food) eltaantunut, pilaantunut
    mennä vanhaksi (e.g. of food, medication, passport) ― to expire

Etymology

[edit]

From Proto-Finnic *vanha. Cognates include Finnish vanha and Estonian vana.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • (Ala-Laukaa) IPA(key): /ˈʋɑnɑ/, [ˈʋɑnɑˑ]
  • (Soikkola) IPA(key): /ˈʋɑnhɑ/, [ˈʋɑnɣ̥ɑ]
  • Rhymes: -ɑnɑ, -ɑnhɑ
  • Hyphenation: van‧ha

Adjective

[edit]

vanha (comparative vanhemp)

  1. old
  2. former
